title: Only One judges alone (Avot 4:8)
hook: a director alone at midnight with the cast list: don't judge alone, for only One judges alone
tomorrow: the money's gone. does the practice go with it?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Rabbi Yose: whoever honors the Torah is honored. Honor the book. Today, a sage on what to do when the call is yours.

A kitchen table after midnight. A stack of audition photos, a laptop open to a blank cast list, cold tea. The student director watched every audition herself. Nobody else was in the room. The list goes up after school tomorrow, and every name on it is her call. She types the last name, hovers over send, and stops. Something about doing this alone sits wrong, and she can't say what. A sage in Pirkei Avot can.
screen: `MIDNIGHT. A BLANK CAST LIST.` → `EVERY NAME IS HER CALL.` → `WHY DOES ALONE FEEL WRONG?`

segments.voice: Rabbi Ishmael, son of Rabbi Yose, says it in two short lines. Don't judge alone, for none judges alone but One. And don't say, accept my view, for they may say that, and not you. The One is God. In this saying, judging by yourself belongs to God alone, because only God sees the whole case: the motive, the history, the part nobody said out loud. Every human judge sees a slice. So the Mishnah builds courts out of more than one person. Elsewhere it sets three judges even for a quarrel over money. Here's the one to tell a friend tonight: in the Mishnah, a dispute about a loan doesn't get one judge. It gets three. The second line is sharper. Don't say, accept my view. Your colleagues, as a group, may say that to you. You, alone, may not say it to them. Even when you're right, rightness doesn't hand you the gavel. That's the answer to the midnight table. The director has the authority. But a cast list is a verdict about people, and this saying treats every verdict as too big for one pair of eyes. So she texts the stage manager a photo of the list. Two minutes later: are you sure about the second lead? She wasn't, it turns out.
screen: `DON'T JUDGE ALONE.` · `ONLY GOD SEES THE WHOLE CASE.` · `EVEN A LOAN GETS THREE JUDGES.` · `DON'T SAY: ACCEPT MY VIEW.` · then, large: `ONLY ONE JUDGES ALONE.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and paper. Write one call you've been making alone this week, a verdict about a person, a plan, a choice, in a single line. Under it, write the name of one person who'd see the part you can't, and rest your eyes on the two lines for the rest of the sit.
screen: `ONE CALL I'M MAKING ALONE.` · `ONE NAME WHO'D SEE MORE.`

segments.voice: Only One judges alone. Rabbi Ishmael's line: judging by yourself belongs to God, so people judge together.
Keep this one: only one judges alone, and it isn't you or me. Thirty days into the rest of Avot.

howItsDone: Jewish courts (a beit din) sit as a panel rather than a single judge, and in study many Jews learn in pairs, a chavruta, so no reading of a text goes unchallenged.

match.prompt: the saying, piece by piece — tap the pairs.

fork.setup: you're grading your study group's shared project, and you're sure one member slacked. the group report is due tonight. what does Rabbi Ishmael's line point to?
options: show your notes to one other member and ask what they saw before writing it up.
write it up yourself; you were there, you saw it, and you're right.
leave it out entirely, since judging anyone is God's job alone.
fork.reveal: the saying doesn't ban judging; courts judge. it bans judging alone. a second pair of eyes is the default, not a weakness.

original.note: Hebrew: don't be a judge alone. yechidi, alone, is the word the saying turns on.

trapdoor: what you thought: a polite tip to ask around before deciding.
what it means: judging by yourself belongs to God, who alone sees the whole case; people judge together.
what a scholar hears: a saying from a world of courts; elsewhere the Mishnah sets three judges even for money cases, and 'accept my view' is the majority's right, not one judge's.
guess: God alone may judge by himself; people judge together
a judge should decide alone to keep the case pure
only one person in a family may settle a quarrel
recall: whoever honors the Torah is honored
Torah isn't a crown or a digging tool

chat.says: cast list for my one-act is due tmrw. i watched every audition. i KNOW who's right. why ask anyone?
options: Because a cast list is a verdict on people. Show one person before it goes up.
Don't ask; you watched every audition, so your view is the one to accept.
Ask the whole cast to vote, so no one can say you judged them.
chat.meaning: Only One judges alone. The director keeps the call, but Avot says no verdict about people should rest on one pair of eyes.

Pirkei Avot.meaning: the Mishnah's book of sages' sayings, the Ethics of the Fathers

Rabbi Ishmael.meaning: a sage of the Mishnah, son of Rabbi Yose

Mishnah.meaning: the early collection of Jewish teaching and law

Torah.meaning: God's teaching; the five books of Moses
